podcast.title: First UK Punk Release (1976)
podcast.body: Stiff Records was the first label to release any punk record in the UK. This historic release was "New Rose" by The Damned on October 22nd, 1976. "In fact, Stiff was the first label to release any kind of punk record in the UK. The date for that was October 22nd, 1976."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 1

podcast.title: Founding (1976)
podcast.body: Stiff Records was a small company founded in 1976 by Dave Robinson and Jake Riviera, completely dedicated to punk music. "This was a small company formed by Dave Robinson and Jake Riviera in 1976 and was totally devoted to punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 1

podcast.title: Sale to Island Records (1983)
podcast.body: Due to financial difficulties and mismanagement, Stiff Records was sold off by 1983, with Island Records acquiring it. "Stiff was terrible at conducting business. They were irresponsible and they bled money and were sold off by 1983. And the buyer? Another indie. Island Records."

podcast.title: British Indie Label
podcast.body: A UK indie label that was a major factor in breaking new music, particularly since the punk era of the 1970s. "There was rough trade, two-tone and stiff, mute, and dozens of others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Association with a Cultural Meme
podcast.body: Stiff Records released "Sex & Drugs & Rock & Roll" by Ian Dury and the Blockheads in 1977. This song is credited with widely popularizing the phrase, turning it into a significant cultural "meme."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Significant Releases
podcast.body: The label released Nick Lowe's debut solo single, "So It Goes," in 1976, and Elvis Costello's debut single, "Less Than Zero." "In 1976, Stiff put out Lo's debut single, so it goes."

podcast.title: First Artist Signed
podcast.body: Stiff Records was a "fierce little UK label" that signed Declan McManus (later Elvis Costello) as its very first artist after he had faced numerous rejections from other labels. This marked the beginning of Costello's professional recording career. "until he managed to be the very first person signed to the new Stiff Records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Elvis Costello

podcast.title: Forefront of Punk and New Wave
podcast.body: Stiff Records was an independent label that positioned itself at the forefront of the punk and new wave movements. Its willingness to embrace unconventional talent led to artists like Lene Lovich, with her quirky style, coming to their attention around 1978. "stiff records, an indie label very much at the forefront of the punk and new wave worlds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Graham Parker's "Mercury Poisoning"
podcast.body: Stiff Records issued Graham Parker's scathing Mercury Records diss track, "Mercury Poisoning," as a one-off single in the UK. "The Mercury diss track was issued as a one off by Stiff Records in the UK."

podcast.title: Jake Riviera's Vision
podcast.body: Stiff Records, under the leadership of Jake Riviera, aimed to quickly release new music to capitalize on the emerging punk rock scene. This urgency led Riviera to arrange for the American band Clover (performing as The Sham Rocks) to secretly back Elvis Costello on his debut album, My Aim Is True, due to Costello's lack of a ready band. "Jake Riviera, the head of the label, wanted to get something out fast to capitalize in this whole punk thing that was happening."

podcast.title: Notable Roster & Business Challenges
podcast.body: The label was known for signing influential artists like Elvis Costello, Madness, The Pogues, and Motörhead. However, Stiff Records struggled with business management, described as "terrible at conducting business," being "irresponsible," and "bleeding money." "Alva's Costello, Madness, the Pog's Motorhead, but Stiff was terrible at conducting business. They were irresponsible and they bled money and were sold off by 1983."

podcast.title: Pioneering Independent Punk
podcast.body: Stiff was a new independent record label that released The Damned's "New Rose" on October 22, 1976, for a budget of £50. This release was historically significant as the first made-in-Britain punk rock record and championed the "do it yourself" approach to music. "Less than two weeks after the pistols signed their EMI deal, a group called the Damned released a 45 on a new label called Stiff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pivotal to British Punk
podcast.body: Stiff Records was a label vital to the breakthrough and establishment of British punk music. Nick Lowe signed with the label to launch his solo career in 1976. "Stiff Records, which would be vital to the breakthrough of British punk."

podcast.title: Promoter of DIY Punk
podcast.body: Stiff Records was instrumental in promoting the "do it yourself" (DIY) punk ethos during the genre's formative years. "perhaps the most important label when it came to pushing DIY punk, do it yourself punk, in the infancy of that music."
